chunks: You cannot offer any excuse before Allāh or before me for wilful killing
because there must be the question of revenge in it.
If you are involved in it by error and you exceed in the use of your whip or sword, or are hard in inflicting punishment,
as sometimes even a blow by the fist or a smaller stroke causes death,
then the haughtiness of your authority should not prevent you from paying the blood price to the successors of the killed person.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: The successors/heirs of the killed person

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between intentional and accidental killing in Islamic jurisprudence according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this directive from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of accountability for rulers, distinguishing between intentional homicide requiring *qisas* (bodily revenge) and accidental killing resulting from judicial or administrative error. He warns Malik al-Ashtar that the arrogance of power (*nakhwat sultanika*) must not deter him from fulfilling the financial compensation (*diyah*) to the heirs, emphasizing that even a ruler is subject to the same legal obligations as any other citizen in cases of error.
